proof_nl:
Let G_{n,r}(q) := (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}). Since each factor 1 - q^i is a nonzero polynomial in Z[q], each (q;q)_m is nonzero, so G_{n,r}(q) is a well-defined element of the rational function field Q(q).

We prove by induction on n that for every integer r with 0 <= r <= n, G_{n,r}(q) is a nonzero polynomial in Z[q] of degree r(n-r).

Base case n = 0: then r = 0, and
G_{0,0}(q) = (q;q)_0 / ((q;q)_0 (q;q)_0) = 1.
This is a nonzero polynomial in Z[q] of degree 0 = 0(0-0).

Induction step: assume the claim has been proved for n-1, and let r satisfy 0 <= r <= n.

If r = 0, then
G_{n,0}(q) = (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_0 (q;q)_n) = 1.
If r = n, then
G_{n,n}(q) = (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_n (q;q)_0) = 1.
In either case G_{n,r}(q) is a nonzero polynomial of degree 0 = r(n-r).

Now assume 0 < r < n. We derive the usual recurrence directly from the definition. Using
(q;q)_{n-r} = (1 - q^{n-r})(q;q)_{n-r-1}
and
(q;q)_r = (1 - q^r)(q;q)_{r-1},
we have in Q(q):

G_{n-1,r}(q)
= (q;q)_{n-1} / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r-1})
= (1 - q^{n-r})(q;q)_{n-1} / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}),

and

q^{n-r} G_{n-1,r-1}(q)
= q^{n-r} (q;q)_{n-1} / ((q;q)_{r-1} (q;q)_{n-r})
= q^{n-r}(1 - q^r)(q;q)_{n-1} / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r}).

Adding these two identities gives

G_{n-1,r}(q) + q^{n-r} G_{n-1,r-1}(q)
= ((1 - q^{n-r}) + q^{n-r}(1 - q^r))(q;q)_{n-1} / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r})
= (1 - q^n)(q;q)_{n-1} / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r})
= (q;q)_n / ((q;q)_r (q;q)_{n-r})
= G_{n,r}(q).

So for 0 < r < n,
G_{n,r}(q) = G_{n-1,r}(q) + q^{n-r} G_{n-1,r-1}(q).

By the induction hypothesis, both G_{n-1,r}(q) and G_{n-1,r-1}(q) are nonzero polynomials in Z[q]. Hence their sum G_{n,r}(q) also lies in Z[q].

Now compute degrees. By induction,
deg G_{n-1,r}(q) = r((n-1)-r) = r(n-r) - r,
and
deg G_{n-1,r-1}(q) = (r-1)(n-r).
Therefore

deg(q^{n-r} G_{n-1,r-1}(q)) = (n-r) + (r-1)(n-r) = r(n-r).

Since r > 0, we have
r(n-r) - r < r(n-r).
Thus the second summand has strictly larger degree than the first. Because G_{n-1,r-1}(q) is nonzero, q^{n-r} G_{n-1,r-1}(q) has a nonzero term of degree r(n-r); the first summand has no term of that degree, so no cancellation is possible. Hence

deg G_{n,r}(q) = r(n-r).
In particular G_{n,r}(q) is nonzero.

This completes the induction. Therefore for all integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient [n choose r]_q is a nonzero polynomial in Z[q] of degree r(n-r).
solver_summary: Induction on n. The cases r = 0 and r = n give the value 1. For 0 < r < n, a direct manipulation of the q-Pochhammer definition yields the recurrence G_{n,r} = G_{n-1,r} + q^{n-r} G_{n-1,r-1}. The induction hypothesis then gives polynomiality, and the second summand has strictly larger degree than the first, so the degree is exactly r(n-r), which also implies nonzeroness.
